title: Semantic Search Engine
blurb: Compare keyword search and embedding search on your own document set, with real retrieval metrics.
brief: Build a search engine over a document collection (articles, docs or notes). Implement a TF-IDF or BM25 baseline, add embedding-based retrieval with chunking and cosine similarity, and optionally combine both. Create a small labeled set of queries with the documents that should be returned, then report recall@k and MRR for every method so you can show, with numbers, when embeddings help.
requirements: Document loading and chunking with configurable size and overlap
Embedding-based retrieval (a local sentence-embedding model or an embeddings API behind a small interface)
Cosine-similarity top-k search over a stored index
A labeled evaluation set and recall@k and MRR (or nDCG) metrics
A comparison table of methods and a short analysis of failure cases
deliverables: Indexing and search modules plus a simple command-line search tool
The evaluation set and a script that regenerates the results table
README with design decisions (chunk size, model choice) justified by the metrics
resume_bullet: Built and evaluated a semantic search engine (TF-IDF/BM25 baseline vs embeddings, recall@k and MRR) over a custom document corpus.
